question.problem:
Find ${e}^{At}$ for $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}].$ *Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $2\pm 3\text{i}.$*
${e}^{At}={e}^{2t}\,\,$ {{field-1}} $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$
{{field-2}} $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$
question.worked_solution:
We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & 6{\alpha }_{1}t \\ -3{\alpha }_{1}t & -{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues or $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=(2+3\text{i})t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=(2-3\text{i})t,
$$

which are complex conjugates. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r((2+3\text{i})t) & ={e}^{(2+3\text{i})t} \\ {\alpha }_{1}(2+3\text{i})t+{\alpha }_{0} & ={e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) \\ (2{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0})+3{\alpha }_{1}\text{i}t & ={e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\text{i}\,{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we equate the real and imaginary parts, and solve for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ 3t{\alpha }_{1}={e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}=\frac{1}{3t}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ {\alpha }_{0}={e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =5\cdot \frac{1}{3t}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\cdot t+{e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{2}{3}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\  & ={e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) \\ -3{\alpha }_{1}t & =-3\cdot \frac{1}{3t}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\cdot t \\  & =-{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}={e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}].
$$
